stories.head: Salesforce buying AI customer support company Cresta
stories.plain: Salesforce is acquiring Cresta, which puts AI voice agents inside live customer calls and links those conversations to CRM data. This extends Salesforce's Agentforce push deeper into real-time service interactions. Any marketer buying or governing customer-service AI needs to watch how this reshapes the vendor landscape and what it means for data ownership.

stories.head: AI-generated answers now top starting point for product research among AI-active shoppers
stories.plain: Impact.com research finds 47% of AI-active U.S. consumers start product searches with an AI-generated answer, beating traditional search at 26%. This is a structural shift in the buyer journey — brands that aren't visible inside AI responses are losing consideration before the shopper ever reaches a website or ad.

stories.head: AI traffic drives 83% more revenue per visit, Adobe research finds
stories.plain: Adobe data shows visitors arriving via AI referrals convert 90% better and generate 83% more revenue per visit than non-AI traffic. This gives marketers a hard business case for investing in generative engine optimization — being named inside AI answers isn't just a vanity metric, it delivers measurably higher-quality buyers.

stories.head: Brandi AI CEO on winning the AI answer, not the search click
stories.plain: Leah Nurik explains how AI assistants decide which brand names to surface and why GEO requires PR and product marketing — not just SEO tactics. As AI-generated answers displace search rankings, this interview offers concrete guidance on what to measure and how to build presence inside AI responses.

stories.head: Only 7% of travelers would let AI act autonomously on their behalf, Parloa survey finds
stories.plain: Parloa's consumer survey reveals a sharp gap: people trust AI to monitor and alert, but only 7% would let an agent take action without approval. Willingness rises among younger consumers and in agent-to-agent scenarios. Marketers building agentic experiences need to design for human confirmation loops or risk losing customer trust.

stories.head: Salesforce buying AI customer support company Cresta for ~$2.7B
stories.plain: Salesforce is acquiring Cresta, which builds AI voice agents that handle and coach live customer calls. At a reported $2.7 billion, this is a major bet on agentic CX — tying phone conversations directly into CRM data and the Agentforce platform. It signals that autonomous agents are now core infrastructure, not an add-on, for enterprise marketing and service stacks.

stories.head: AI-generated answers now top starting point for product research, beating traditional search
stories.plain: Impact.com research finds 47% of AI-active U.S. shoppers now begin product searches with an AI-generated response, compared to only 26% starting with traditional search results. This is a tipping point for how brands get discovered — if you're not visible inside AI answers, you're missing the new front door of the buyer journey.

stories.head: Adobe research: AI-referred traffic converts 90% better and drives 83% more revenue per visit
stories.plain: Adobe's data shows visitors arriving from AI tools are far more purchase-ready than those from other channels — 90% higher conversion rates and 83% more revenue per visit. This gives marketers a hard financial case for investing in generative engine optimization and understanding which AI surfaces are sending buyers their way.

stories.head: Brandi AI CEO explains how to win AI-answer visibility — GEO needs PR and product marketing, not SEO tactics
stories.plain: Leah Nurik explains that AI assistants choose brands based on credibility signals — third-party mentions, clear positioning, and product marketing clarity — not keyword density. She lays out what marketers should measure instead of search rank. Practical guidance for anyone trying to understand why their brand does or doesn't appear in AI-generated recommendations.

stories.head: Survey: consumers open to AI travel agents but only 7% will let AI act autonomously on their behalf
stories.plain: Parloa's consumer research reveals a sharp gap between AI trust and AI autonomy: people want AI to monitor and inform, but only 7% will grant it permission to act without asking. Willingness rises steeply among younger groups. This sets a real-world consent boundary that agentic platform designers and governance teams must plan around.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Answers Replace the Search Bar as Discovery's Front Door
body: AI-generated answers have overtaken traditional search as the primary starting point for product research among the most active digital shoppers. Data showing AI traffic delivers 83% more revenue per visit than other channels means this is no longer a future-state concern — it is a present-tense reallocation of commercial intent.

The strategic implication is that winning an AI recommendation slot matters more than ranking on a results page. Brands must now optimise for how models summarise & cite them, not just for crawlable keywords — a discipline Brandi AI's CEO calls 'winning the answer, not the click.'

Agile Brand · Brandi AI CEO on winning the answer

themes.head: Agentic Autonomy Runs Into a Trust Ceiling
body: The industry is actively redesigning martech operations around autonomous AI agents, yet consumer willingness to grant that autonomy lags far behind vendor ambition. A Parloa survey found only 7% of travellers would let AI act on their behalf — a gap that exposes the difference between AI-assisted decisions and AI-executed ones.

Teamily AI's vision of an 'agentic, appless internet' and Asana's agentic work-management push show supply-side enthusiasm is at a peak. The practical constraint for marketers is designing human-in-the-loop checkpoints that preserve speed gains while staying inside the trust envelope consumers will actually accept.

themes.head: AI Adoption's Dirty Secret: Nobody Can Prove It Works
body: Most marketers report that AI is working, yet few have the measurement infrastructure to substantiate the claim. This credibility gap — documented in martech surveys and reinforced by practitioner commentary on pattern-finding versus meaning-making — means AI ROI is largely anecdotal at the leadership level where budget decisions are made.

The risk is a coming correction: when CFOs demand proof, teams that skipped the measurement design phase will be exposed. Marketers are being advised to define weaknesses and benchmarks before deploying AI, not after, so there is a counterfactual to point to when the board asks.

themes.head: CX Consolidation: Big Platforms Absorb Voice & Service AI
body: Salesforce's acquisition of Cresta — a voice AI specialist — signals that the era of best-of-breed point solutions for customer experience is compressing into platform-level bundles. The deal adds real-time, phone-based AI coaching to Salesforce's already expanding CX stack, raising the integration bar for independent vendors.

For martech buyers, this wave of consolidation means fewer standalone AI tools will survive as credible enterprise options; procurement decisions made today may be obsoleted by a platform announcement within 12–18 months. Evaluating vendor roadmaps for acquisition likelihood is becoming a standard due-diligence step.
ev: Agile Brand · Salesforce acquires Cresta voice AI

themes.head: Change Management, Not Code, Is the Real AI Bottleneck
body: Deployment is no longer the hard part; getting teams to change how they actually work after deployment is. Multiple pieces this month converge on the same finding: AI tools that lack structured adoption programmes stall out, with staff reverting to old workflows within weeks of rollout.

The practical advice clusters around sequencing — establishing a content or data destination before reaching for a prompt, and redesigning incentives so that using AI tools is the path of least resistance rather than an extra step. Leadership behaviour, not licence count, is now the leading indicator of AI maturity.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack — discovery, service, measurement & operations — AI is shifting from a capability question to a governance & trust question, and the marketers who build that infrastructure now will be the ones who can prove value when scrutiny arrives.
